correctness.rationale: For any pair at underlying cycle distance at most \(2r\), the interior midpoint is forced until a consecutive selected pair occurs; \(r\ge2\) then grows the consecutive block around the circle. The converse follows from the metric triangle inequality. Cyclic gaps \(\ge2r+1\) correspond bijectively to proper convex \(k\)-sets, with each unmarked k-set counted \(k\) times across \(n\) starting vertices, giving the exact \(n/k\) binomial coefficient. Full set is separate. A standard-library adjacency/propagation/composition checker confirms sample cases but is not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2021 work invokes a general 2-connected chordal-graph pair-hull theorem that covers path powers; the new claim was narrowed to cycle powers. Nonchordal \(C_6^2\) has induced four-cycles, so the chordal theorem cannot imply the claim there. The 2026 generic exact algorithms work on arbitrary inputs but provide no closed cycle-power characterization or polynomial. The present domain includes infinitely many such nonchordal graphs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A 2-connected chordal-graph theorem implies pair percolation on path powers, so no originality is asserted for path powers. It is inapplicable to nonchordal cycle powers. The 2026 tree/path recurrences and threshold-graph formulas do not imply this all-cardinality formula on cycle powers, and its general algorithms are not the asserted closed theorem.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Ordinary P3 convexity is equivalent to threshold-two bootstrap stability. The exact cyclic-gap criterion implies all proper stable sets are independent sets of the higher cycle power. Searches for both original language and bootstrap/packing aliases did not locate a prior two-parameter full classification. The general neighbour-count definition alone does not supply the forcing and circle-counting argument.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Related public mathematical search hits for cycle powers concern topological neighborhood/cut complexes, not P3-convexity enumerators. No exact precomputed convex-set table or database of these coefficients was identified. The absence of a matching search hit is not itself a novelty proof.
searches: P3 convexity polynomial exact count all convex sets powers of cycles C_n^r r>=2, two-neighbour bootstrap packing formula with gap 2r+1

originality.rationale: Inspected the full 2026 counting paper and relevant sections of a 2021 primary paper with a stronger hull theorem for 2-connected chordal graphs. The path-power implication is known and excluded. The present theorem covers nonchordal powers of cycles and their full cardinality polynomials, neither stated nor implied by the inspected sources. Mathematical-record queries returned closest graph-power results on unrelated topological complexes; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Full text of indexed cycle-power topology papers not inspected; their visible results concern other invariants but unobserved connections cannot be excluded.

Independent literature priority review has not been performed.

value.rationale: A recently studied #P-hard counting problem obtains a complete uniform structural solution for a two-parameter, generally nonchordal cycle-power family, beyond known tree/threshold and chordal pair-hull results. It computes every cardinality coefficient and the maximum proper convex size; the radius-two transition is sharp and mathematically motivated by threshold-two propagation.
